title: Children's eye exam
what: The doctor checks how well your child sees and examines the eyes. For little ones, pictures and toys are used.
why: For routine checkups, or if your child squints, sits close to things, has a turning eye, or complains about their eyes.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes; with dilating drops, up to 1 to 1.5 hours
tell_doctor: What you notice: squinting, eye rubbing, head tilting, a turning eye
If relatives have nearsightedness, a squint, or other eye conditions

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: Choose a time when your child is not hungry or sleepy.

prepare.title: Talk to your child
prepare.text: Tell your child it will be a game with pictures and a little flashlight.

prepare.title: Drops
prepare.text: If dilating drops are used, vision will be blurry for a few hours afterward. Plan your day.

bring: Your child's glasses, if they have them
steps: The doctor asks about your concerns
Your child names pictures or letters on a chart
Each eye is checked in turn, with the other covered
A machine measures how the eye focuses, without touching it
Sometimes drops are put in, and you wait 20 to 40 minutes
The doctor looks into the eyes with a light and a lens
feel: The drops may sting a little
After the drops, light seems bright and close-up vision is worse. This passes in a few hours
after: If drops were used, a cap or sunglasses help outdoors
The doctor will say if glasses are needed and when to come back
red_flags: The eye turns red and painful after the drops, or your child cannot open it: see a doctor

faq.q: At what age is vision checked?
faq.a: The first exam is usually in the first months of life, then at routine checkups.
The drops relax the eye muscles, so the doctor can see more exactly if glasses are needed.

faq.q: My child does not know letters. How will they be tested?
faq.a: For little ones, there are picture charts and machines that need no answers.

reminders.text: Your child's eye exam is in 2 hours. Bring their glasses, if they have them.
